subject.title: RFC: Standard Hosting Profiles and Ready Check

question: Should OpenClaw core own named hosting profiles and make selected-profile conformance part of its stable readiness contract?
rationale: The proposal creates permanent public configuration, status, readiness, and release-conformance obligations; code and document review cannot determine whether maintainers want core to carry that support boundary.

options.title: Accept Readiness Foundation
options.body: Approve the canonical condition model and default local projection first, then evaluate additional profiles after Docker and operational proof.

options.title: Accept Full Profile Catalog
options.body: Approve all five built-in profiles and their predicates as one stable core support contract.

options.title: Keep Checks Host-Owned
options.body: Decline named core profiles and retain topology-specific readiness assertions in hosting integrations or downstream supervisors.

recommendation.title: Accept Readiness Foundation
recommendation.body: Approve the canonical condition model and default local projection first, then evaluate additional profiles after Docker and operational proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Their commits established the repository's RFC lifecycle, making them the strongest available routing candidate for moving this proposal through discussion and acceptance.
